resharper_csharp_int_align_binary_expressions #

Align similar code in columns — Binary expressions. Implemented for the conditional chain and not for the rest of the key: with it on, the oracle also pads adjacent local variable declarations whose initializers are binary, at every operator of the chain — var first = flag > 1 && other > 2; beside var secondName = flag > 100000 && other > 2; comes back with both the > and the && in a column. Measured at the ternary-chain work on constructs/alignment/int-align-ternary.cs, and it is what keeps this key at Tier D now that the chain layout no longer does. ⚠ Adjacent assignments with binary right-hand sides do not move, so 'declarations' is the measured population and not a guess.

Typetrue / false
Defaultfalse
Default known fromthe Rider export, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two

resharper_csharp_int_align_fix_in_adjacent #

Align similar code in columns — Fix column alignment in adjacent lines. Measured inert on a stronger probe than the recorded "no answer while no run exists". false one key away from the export returns an 18-file probe byte-identical, which is the weak reading. It is also byte-identical with int_align_variables = true and int_align_fields = true supplied — so adjacent declarations really are padded into a column and the neighbours it claims to govern exist — and byte-identical again with allow_far_alignment = true added on top of that. Two second keys tried, and the key moves nothing in either, so this is not merely masking.
